News.title: I Am Maximus emulates Red Rum to seal status as a Grand National great
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of Grand National day at Aintree, with 34 runners going to post for the world’s most famous steeplechase.

With less punishing obstacles and a field full of contenders with Grade One form, the race’s complexion has changed over the last few decades but interest levels remain as high as ever.

There is nowhere else to start than with JP McManus’ green-and-gold battalion; the Irish owner accounts for four of the top six horses in the betting market.

I Am Maximus evidently has the class and course form having finished first and second in each of the last two Nationals, with Willie Mullins’ top jockey Paul Townend on board. However, he carries top weight which could prove difficult to overcome in a field with such depth.

Punters have followed Jagwar over cliffs, he is a horse with so much ability but a horrible habit of finishing second, notably to fellow McManus horse Johnnywho in the Ultima Handicap Chase at Cheltenham. Iroko finished in midfield in that race, but has long been considered a National plot after running on to finish fourth last year.

Speaking of plots, the Skelton team commands respect in these blue-chip handicaps and their chance is Panic Attack, tipped by our very own Marcus Armytage to become the first mare to win the race in 75 years. Dinoblue had too much speed for her in the Mares’ Chase at Cheltenham, but Panic Attack is back in handicap company today after successes in the Paddy Power Gold Cup and Coral Gold Cup earlier in the season.

Bobbyjo winner Grangeclare West is another serious player for Mullins with son Paddy in the saddle, while Monty’s Star for Henry De Bromhead has a Gold Cup fourth on his CV and can be relied on to run his race

Before the main event, there are three Grade Ones on the card: Salvator Mundi is a short price for the Hallgarten & Novum Wines Maghull Novices’ Chase, there is the middle distance Turners Mersey Novices’ Hurdle followed by the Jet2 Liverpool Hurdle for the older stayers.

News.title: There is an inescapable sense that Arsenal are blowing the title
News.content:
In one technical area, Arteta’s childhood team-mate from San Sebastián, Andoni Iraola, a cheerful, easy-going Basque, was giving his old acquaintance a tactical masterclass. Then there was Arteta, a brooding and explosive Basque, committed to his Arsenal creed, watching his players being picked off in possession. Bournemouth pressed fearlessly. Scott and Ryan Christie ran the show. Arteta did not – could not – change the approach and so the drama played out.

Afterwards the Arsenal manager chewed over the details, talking darkly about “some very basic things that we did extremely badly”, but declined to elaborate. He refused to feel sorry for himself but did, nonetheless, mention some of the key men who are still injured. On the other hand, Iraola, shrugged and pointed out that anyone who watched his team knew that they embraced the press, accepted the risk, and chased the reward. Today their ship finally came in – there have been seven draws in the 12 straight Premier League games Bournemouth have now gone undefeated.

This was a fabulous game – full of tension and unexpected twists. One wonders if Sporting CP, due at the Emirates on Wednesday for the resumption of their Champions League quarter-final tie, will take note. Perhaps they had always intended to approach the second leg differently, but the combination of a home crowd determined to urge the team forward, and then Arteta’s insistence on the short passing game, presents opportunities.

The win in Lisbon in the 91st minute is the only Arsenal triumph in the past four games in four different competitions. Three defeats going back to the Carabao Cup final on March 22 – all of them different, all of them pregnant with meaning – and now the closing weeks of the season presents an Arsenal psychodrama like none other.

It is gripping stuff, no less absorbing than the relegation calamity unfolding over at Tottenham Hotspur. Another injury to Riccardo Calafiori meant only the second league start of the season for Myles Lewis-Skelly – and he was among the better performers for Arteta. But others in his side failed notably to rise to the occasion.

Arteta felt that too and went early with his changes. After 53 minutes, and with the score level, he abandoned his faith in Noni Madueke, Kai Havertz and Gabriel Martinelli – and sent on three very good alternatives. But he would not abandon the system – and it was the system which was giving Bournemouth their opportunities.

“A game of cat and mouse” was Iraola’s elegant grip of the idiom to describe the pressing game of the likes of Eli Junior Kroupi, Evanilson and Brazilian Rayan. Could Arteta have changed it? To go long would have meant relying on Viktor Gyökeres as the target-man fulcrum, and the Arsenal manager seems unprepared to do that. The £64m striker dispatched a first-half penalty but otherwise nothing has changed. He can do certain things, but conjuring a match-winning, title-defining goal from nowhere is not one of them.

News.title: Rusty Red Roses still comfortable winners against Ireland in Women’s Six Nations
News.content:
After the high of last year’s World Cup, England were somewhat rusty in this Women’s Six Nations opener. But a five-try win against Ireland nonetheless suggested they have enough firepower to ease towards another Six Nations title.

Being crowned world champions capped off a generational moment for the women’s game and it is hard to know what there is left for the Red Roses to conquer. John Mitchell’s side are now on a 34-match winning streak and are unbeaten in the Six Nations since 2018. They are already a team of standard setters, record breakers and history makers. Yet there remains a relentless drive to achieve more.

In front of a 77,120-strong crowd inside the Allianz Stadium – a record for a Women’s Six Nations match – they laboured to a bonus-point victory, but it was still another comfortable win.

Mitchell was expecting his Red Roses to be “clunky” in places. It was as if he had a crystal ball. With a quartet of their usual forwards missing through pregnancy, including their influential leader Zoe Stratford who was on punditry duties for the BBC, England certainly lacked their usual crispness.

Given what they have achieved on the world stage, the expectation on this England team perhaps overwhelmed them at times, while tournament-ending injuries to Morwenna Talling and Natasha Hunt soured the occasion. “Naturally we’re a new team, it’s a new start and there’s going to be plenty of learnings. Some people went off plan,” Mitchell conceded.

England’s attempts at spreading the ball wide were thwarted by a well-drilled Ireland side who were impressive in defence but still stifled by their opponent’s sheer physicality.

A try from Amy Cokayne and a double from Sarah Bern proved enough to kill off Ireland in a lacklustre first half, before England’s back line clicked in patches after the break, with Jess Breach and Ellie Kildunne dotting down. In her first outing as England captain, Meg Jones was pivotal.

News.title: Grand National runners and riders 2026: Full horse guide
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of Grand National day at Aintree, with 34 runners going to post for the world’s most famous steeplechase.

With less punishing obstacles and a field full of contenders with Grade One form, the race’s complexion has changed over the last few decades but interest levels remain as high as ever.

There is nowhere else to start than with JP McManus’ green-and-gold battalion; the Irish owner accounts for four of the top six horses in the betting market.

I Am Maximus evidently has the class and course form having finished first and second in each of the last two Nationals, with Willie Mullins’ top jockey Paul Townend on board. However, he carries top weight which could prove difficult to overcome in a field with such depth.

Punters have followed Jagwar over cliffs, he is a horse with so much ability but a horrible habit of finishing second, notably to fellow McManus horse Johnnywho in the Ultima Handicap Chase at Cheltenham. Iroko finished in midfield in that race, but has long been considered a National plot after running on to finish fourth last year.

Speaking of plots, the Skelton team commands respect in these blue-chip handicaps and their chance is Panic Attack, tipped by our very own Marcus Armytage to become the first mare to win the race in 75 years. Dinoblue had too much speed for her in the Mares’ Chase at Cheltenham, but Panic Attack is back in handicap company today after successes in the Paddy Power Gold Cup and Coral Gold Cup earlier in the season.

Bobbyjo winner Grangeclare West is another serious player for Mullins with son Paddy in the saddle, while Monty’s Star for Henry De Bromhead has a Gold Cup fourth on his CV and can be relied on to run his race

Before the main event, there are three Grade Ones on the card: Salvator Mundi is a short price for the Hallgarten & Novum Wines Maghull Novices’ Chase, there is the middle distance Turners Mersey Novices’ Hurdle followed by the Jet2 Liverpool Hurdle for the older stayers.

News.title: Rory McIlroy surges six clear and sets Masters record after stunning display
News.content:
McIlroy sounded without fear about the prospect. “I’ve built up a nice cushion at this point. I guess my mindset is just trying to keep playing well and keeping my foot on the gas,” he said. “Don’t protect it. Go out and play freely, keep swinging. A big part of the lesson from the 2011 Masters to the 2011 US Open was: don’t get protective. Go out there and keep playing, keep trying to make birdies, stay as trusting and as committed as possible.”

McIlroy knows his pursuers well. In fact, he knows Patrick Reed only too well. The divisive American saw off McIlroy in the last pairing in 2018 to don his Green Jacket. And then, three years ago, McIlroy took a little revenge over Reed at the Dubai Desert Classic in an almighty ding-dong that involved the American throwing a tee at the Northern Irishman and a feud developing through the media.

It could still be delicious and following his 69, Reed agreed. “It’s one of those golf courses that if you go out and you post a low number, you just never know,” he said. “That’s the thing about this course, when it starts playing this firm and fast. Just have to wait and see what the weekend entails. At the same time I love the position I put myself in. Hopefully I can go out and have a good day tomorrow and have a good shot going into Sunday.”

One shot back of second is McIlroy’s Ryder Cup partner Tommy Fleetwood. The Englishman conjured two eagles in his 68 and with only two blemishes on his card – on the first and last – he will be relishing the challenge of going two better here than two years ago and one better than his two runner-up finishes in the majors.

News.title: Bath break Northampton hearts on one of European club rugby’s great nights
News.content:
“We have not spoken about that game at all,” van Graan added. “An amazing thing about this group, you have heard me say it maybe a thousand times, we always start on zero. We took our learnings back in December, just after Christmas, they were better than us and we learned from it and moved on to the next week. They are a team we respect a lot and are currently playing some fantastic rugby.

“They have some of the best players in the Premiership, they score some fantastic tries and they played in last season’s Champions Cup final in Cardiff against Bordeaux and this is their third quarter-final in a row in this competition. So it is a team with some big history in this competition, but all that matters is what happens at 8pm on Friday night. It is a knockout game, and it is going to be a great occasion.”

Northampton were the first side to book their place in the final eight having beaten Castres 49-41 at Franklin’s Gardens in a high-scoring affair last Friday night. Northampton are looking to go one step better than they did in this competition last season, when they lost in the final to Bordeaux. This is the third consecutive season Northampton have reached the quarter-finals of this competition, having beaten the Bulls and Castres in the previous two seasons. Phil Dowson’s side have been boosted by the returns of England internationals Alex Mitchell and Fin Smith to the matchday squad.

The winner of this tie will face either Bordeaux or Toulouse in the semi-finals. Kick-off from The Rec is at 8pm.

News.title: I wanted to switch my broadband provider. I had no idea what I was letting myself in for
News.content:
The email was offering me an upgrade to ‘Full Fibre 100’, with speeds of up to 100Mbps for the same price. This package was costing me £53.50 a month, and if you think that sounds expensive, you would be correct.

A quick browse on rival Virgin Media’s website revealed that I could get Gigabit speeds, ten times as fast as what Sky was offering me, for £30.99 per month – increasing to £35.99 next year.

I’m a writer, not a mathematician, but it doesn’t take a genius to figure out that Sky’s £53.50 for 67Mbps (or 100Mbps if I upgraded) was a worse deal than Virgin’s £30.99 for ten times the speed.

In Sky’s defence, every broadband and mobile provider is guilty of this ‘loyalty penalty’. While there are consumer protections in the UK for home and car insurance, preventing companies from offering better deals to new customers than existing ones, this doesn’t apply to broadband or mobile networks.

I’ll also say that I received an email from Sky prior to them telling me about the speed boost, which said I was going to be out of contract soon. So the company did at least try to warn me.

A warning to all – expect a lot of calls

Sports.title: ‘I wanted to go there’ – Richarlison reveals transfer talks with European giant to play with idol tattooed on his back
Sports.content:
RICHARLISON revealed bold plans as he pushed for a move to join his Brazilian idol at Paris Saint-Germain.

The Tottenham Hotspur forward has even dedicated his back to fellow Brazilian Neymar with a mural tattoo.





So, when Kylian Mbappe was set to leave PSG and the Champions League holders came calling, he was ready to pick up his life and move to Paris.

In an interview with France Football, Richarlison said: “I have had contact with PSG on several occasions.

“Every time Mbappe was about to leave, [the directors] approached me.

“Once, my agent even went to discuss things in the offices in Paris.”

The Brazilian has scored nine times this season for the struggling Lilywhites.

The 28-year-old striker admitted: “I wanted to go there, we talked about it together with Neymar during the Selecao gatherings.

“It didn’t work out, unfortunately, it’s a shame.

“It would have been incredible to play in Paris with him and the other Brazilians.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Spurs are in deep waters after falling into the drop zone – following West Ham‘s BIG win over Wolves.

They face Sunderland away on Sunday in a game crucial for their survival.

But they do have some hope as it will also be Roberto de Zerbi‘s first game leading Spurs.

When the French media asked Richarlison about his tattoo he revealed why the faces of Ronaldo and Neymar are superimposed next to his own and a Brazilian flag.

Richarlison said: “I love Neymar with all my heart.



“I got Neymar’s face tattooed on my back. I also have Ronaldo and Pele’s signature.

“One day, Pele told me that I had made Brazil smile.

“Coming from the King, it was magical. I got that phrase tattooed on my back, with his dedication.”

Sports.title: Brentford 2 Everton 2: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall’s last-gasp equaliser has huge ramifications in race for Champions League
Sports.content:
IGOR THIAGO is the man who cannot miss right now.

But even the Brentford talisman’s two-goal heroics – intentional or not – were not enough to take the points here as Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall salvaged a late point for the Toffees.





Fresh off the back of his maiden strike for Brazil, Samba star Thiago had netted for the 20th and 21st time in the Premier League this term here to put the Bees on the verge of victory.

He knew next to nothing about his second effort, which had ruled out Beto’s leveller, as a shot from team-mate Michael Kayode flew in off him.

It looked set to send Keith Andrews’ side level with fifth-placed Liverpool, but then Dewsbury-Hall reeled them back in with his injury-time blast.

The fact that Brentford and Everton went into this game in seventh and eighth, both on 46 points and three off the Champions League spots was remarkable.

If anyone had that on their bingo cards before the season began, they are lying.

Andrews had never managed before when he became Thomas Frank’s shock successor in the summer at Brentford, who sold the likes of Bryan Mbeumo and Yoane Wissa.

Yet the Irishman has confounded expectations in a stunning debut season, which gives him a strong chance of being the league’s manager of the year.

David Moyes was obviously far more of a sure thing.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But given how dreary Everton have been in recent campaigns, the fact the experienced Scot has them flying so high comes as a surprise too.

His Toffees side were caught napping inside two minutes here though when Kevin Schade raced onto Dango Ouattara’s through ball into the penalty box.

Speedy Schade attempted to go round Everton stopper Jordan Pickford, and went down when the England star caught him with an outstretched foot.



Rookie ref Farai Hallam, officiating just his third Premier League game, correctly pointed to the spot.

It allowed Thiago to keep up his stunning season – which saw him score for Brazil against Croatia last month – as the burly striker fired into the far corner.

But Everton responded from their sloppy start well.

Jarrad Branthwaite fired a warning shot with a 20-yard blast that whistled wide.

Then Bees stopper Caoimhin Kelleher pulled off a tremendous double save to resist, first, a deflect strike from Idrissa Gueye and Beto on the follow-up afterwards.



Brentford were well aware of Beto’s qualities, as confirmed by a rare interview from their owner Matthew Benham earlier this season.

Speaking at the MLT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference 2026, numbers-guy Benham used Beto as an example of how Brentford view players differently to others.

The 57-year-old was talking about how the Guinea-Bissau striker had missed three one-on-ones in this fixture last season, which had prompted derision over his quality.

Yet Benham said: “Any decent data model worth its salt would give Beto an upgrade (when evaluating him).



“That is the case for any player who happens to make three one-on-ones in a single game, even if they happen to miss them.

“Typically for a one-on-one, the odds are 50/50 that you will score. You might say he’s less efficient but the fact he is getting the positions for the shot is more important to us.”

As if to prove Benham’s point, it was Beto who put Everton back on level terms with 26 minutes played.

Keane Lewis-Potter was outmuscled by Jake O’Brien – the only known current Premier League player with type-one Diabetes – out wide.

The inspirational defender then cut the ball back to Gueye, whose floated cross was nodded in by Beto for his fourth in five games.



It was then Brentford’s turn to seize the initiative and they came close to reclaiming the lead, hitting the crossbar twice.

Both came from headers, the first from Schade before the break and then second from captain Nathan Collins after it.

Dewsbury-Hall should have put Everton back ahead when sent clean through but lacked the composure to beat Kelleher.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Thiago thought he had won it with his flukey second, which made him Brentford’s highest-ever scorer in a single Premier League season.

But then ex-Chelsea man Dewsbury-Hall made amends by smashing in with moments to spare.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Man City’s Premier League title run-ins compared with Pep Guardiola’s side’s fate in their own hands
Sports.content:
THE Premier League title race has been blown wide open after Arsenal fell to a shock defeat to Bournemouth.

Mikel Arteta had asked home fans to arrive early to create an atmosphere at the Emirates, but conceding to Eli Junior Kroupi set the tone for a disappointing defeat in North London.





Viktor Gyokeres equalised from the spot in the 35th minute following a controversial penalty call for handball.

However, Arteta’s side lacked the firepower to pop the Cherries’ defence, and eventually found themselves conceding to England World Cup hopeful Alex Scott as he scored the winner in the 74th minute.

Arteta described the defeat as a “big punch in the face” as boos rang out around the Emirates at full-time as the Arsenal faithful felt the déjà vu of being in this spot before.

The Gunners had a nine-point gap to Manchester City starting the day, and that has not grown, while the goal difference value between the sides has shrunk to six goals.



But with City now two games in hand before they play Chelsea on Sunday and Arsenal next week, the title race has swung in the Etihad outfit’s favour.

If Pep Guardiola‘s side win all of their remaining league games, the title will be theirs once again.

City have to be perfect over their next eight games, while Arsenal will look to keep the pressure on across their final six.

Should City beat Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, then next week’s clash between the rivals on April 12 could be decisive for where the title heads at the end of the season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Arsenal will have to contend with the second leg of their Champions League quarter-final against Sporting Lisbon, in which they hold a 1-0 lead after leaving it late to win in Portugal last week, meaning they will lack the week of rest City will have after this weekend.

If they win, Guardiola’s side would still trail by three points with a game in hand.

City will then have back-to-back away games against Burnley and Everton to contend with, sandwiching their FA Cup semi-final against Southampton.

Arsenal’s next game after the crunch title bout will see them host Newcastle.

Following that the Gunners will have to deal with back-to-back north London derbies against Fulham and West Ham, both of which will come after potential Champions League semi-final ties.



Meanwhile, City will approach the final two fixtures of the season after playing Euro chasers Brentford.

The two sides realign their schedules on May 9, with Arsenal playing Burnley in their final home game of the season and City away to Bournemouth.

The final day will then see Arsenal go back to their roots by going to South London to play Crystal Palace, with City back at home hosting top-five chasing Aston Villa.

This year’s title could come down to the final day once again, a familiar scenario for Guardiola during his time at City.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It would be the seventh title the Manchester club have won since Guardiola’s arrival, reclaiming the crown in what could be the Spaniard’s final season in charge.



For Arsenal, it would be a first league title for 23 years.

Sports.title: Burnley 0 Brighton 2: Clarets’ fate all-but sealed as Mats Wieffer double keeps Seagulls’ Champions League hopes alive
Sports.content:
FABIAN HURZELER has admitted it will take something special to tempt him away from Brighton.

Mats Wieffer’s double at Burnley kept the Seagulls firmly in the hunt for Europe.





And not even an approach from one of the Premier League’s genuine heavyweights is likely to lure Hurzeler away if his side secure a place in a Uefa competition for the second time in four seasons.

Wieffer’s strikes, which bookended another forgettable clash at Turf Moor, moved the visitors to within a point of seventh-placed Brentford and two behind faltering Chelsea in sixth.

But while Hurzeler’s men dream of foreign shores, sorry Burnley are plummeting straight back towards the Championship less than 12 months after blazing a trail out of the second tier.



Scott Parker’s side are now 12 points adrift of safety with six games remaining.

Manchester City, Aston Villa and Arsenal all feature on their schedule between now and the end of the campaign.

They showed the odd flash of promise and twice had goals ruled out for offside.

But there was not enough to suggest they stand a chance of completing what would be a miraculous great escape.



And, as Hurzeler’s body language suggested throughout a contest high on industry but low on genuine quality, Brighton were far from their swashbuckling best.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Parker has been feasting on slim pickings since leading Burnley back into the Premier League.

But, as he searches for something to salvage from what has been a miserable campaign, the beleaguered 45 year old can at least point to draws against the likes of Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal’s conquerors Bournemouth.

The only trouble is, with the Clarets kicking off searching for only their second win in 12 outings, that is unlikely to satisfy a fanbase which spent six campaigns rubbing shoulders with the best in the business.

Making four changes to the starting 11 thumped 3-1 by Fulham before the international break, Parker hoped to spark some sort of reaction.



The the one he initially got was not what he was hoping for, with Hjalmar Ekdal forcing Martin Dubravka to head clear after blasting the ball towards his keeper.

And Danny Welbeck spurned a good chance to turn it home at the far post after being found by Yankuba Minteh.

Typically for Burnley, when they did manage to piece together a promising move, Jaidon Anthony saw an early effort ruled out for offside after straying just beyond his marker.



Brighton always carried a threat going forward. But they also looked vulnerable at the back with a corner nearly sneaking in at Bart Verbruggen’s front stick.

Minteh was at the heart of everything good about the Seagulls during the first half.

Unfortunately for the Gambian, he had forgotten to bring his shooting boots.

After flashing across Dubravka’s six-yard box, he made a hash of things when presented with a decent chance of his own and failed to make a clean connection.



Minteh was in the thick of things again as Burnley’s effectiveness began to wane.

This time, he waited far too long to unleash a shot after teasing the hosts’ rearguard and was eventually smothered out.

Brighton midfielder Diego Gomez gave the crowd something to get excited about after theatrically claiming and winning a free-kick, following a challenge from Maxime Esteve, which his team also made a hash of.

It summed up the action during the opening period, with both sets of players occasionally promising plenty but failing to produce the killer final touch.



And the boos cranked up another notch when referee Thomas Bramall called a halt to proceedings to allow Jack Hinshelwood to receive treatment for a head injury when Burnley were going on the counter-attack.

The mood among the home fans turned even sourer two minutes before the interval when Brighton finally engineered the breakthrough their work just about deserved.

Predictably, Minteh was involved in the build-up by sending Pascal Gross scampering down the touchline.

With Burnley failing to impede his progress, the German had all the time in the world to assess his options.



When he spotted Wieffer lurking unmarked inside the area, Gross picked out the Dutchman with a peach of a pass before wheeling away in celebration when he watched his team-mate beat Dubravka.

Burnley had a chance to draw level almost immediately but Lesley Ugochukwu sliced horribly wide.

The Clarets were denied by the assistant referee’s flag for a second time just after the interval.

Having been given a pep talk by Parker, they began the second period in positive fashion.



And it looked to have paid dividends when Verbruggen parried James Ward-Prowse’s set piece straight to Bashir Humphreys.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He found the back of the net but saw his celebrations cut short after making the same mistake as Anthony and edging too far forward.

Wieffer emptied the ground on the stroke of full-time with a lovely finish after a terrible defensive mix-up by Burnley’s backline, sweeping the ball past Dubravka when Yasin Ayari took advantage of their failure to hack clear.

Sports.title: Gutted Mikel Arteta blasts Arsenal took ‘punch in the face’ as Gunners’ Premier League title bid rocked by Bournemouth
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA said Arsenal took a “big punch in the face” as their title bid was rocked by defeat to Bournemouth.

The Gunners stumbled once again and blew the title race wide open as goals from Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott rendered Viktor Gyokeres’ first-half penalty meaningless.





Manchester City, who have two games in hand on Arsenal, can now close the gap at the top of the table to just six points with a win over Chelsea on Sunday.

Arteta said: “It’s like a big punch in the face. That’s what I said to the boys.

“Now it’s about how we react to that.

“Because game on, we are going to require big experience, a lot of fight and to be very clear on how we are going to approach that.



“There’s no grey areas. We are in or we are out.

“We need to be very, very, very strong and determined to approach it in a different way than we’ve done today, especially when the game wasn’t going our way.”

Arsenal, who face Sporting in their Champions League quarter-final second-leg on Wednesday, are watching their season crumble around them.

The north Londoners have now lost three of their last four games, bowing out of the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup in that period.



And their title charge is now faltering once again, having thrown away the league in years past and racked up three consecutive second-placed finishes in the last three seasons.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Arteta had asked the Arsenal fans to bring the noise to help finally push his side over the line.

But a lacklustre performance from his players left him apologising to the Emirates faithful.

He added: “If the atmosphere, the fans, the support, the energy in the stadium is the best in the world. We have a much better chance.



“I don’t think that there’s any other possibility to perform better than when you have that kind of support, but then we have to respond.

“We had moments in the first half where we did it and there were other moments that we were not at our level.

“So we have to apologise to the fans and improve.”

Bournemouth, meanwhile, extended their unbeaten run to 12 GAMES with victory over the floundering Gunners.



The Cherries can now look above them in the hope of achieving a dream European place for the first time in the club’s history.

But Matchwinner Alex Scott knows that is no easy task.

The midfielder said: “It’s not really on our minds.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We know how close it can be between 13th and 14th and seventh, eighth is really tight.

“So it’s down to us to keep winning games, keep getting points, and we’ll see how far we can go at the end of the season.”

Sports.title: Chelsea fans joke Liam Rosenior needs to be sacked if Blues WIN against Man City – ‘Even a draw should be sackable’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans are caught in a pickle ahead of Sunday’s league game against Manchester City.

A win against Pep Guardiola‘s side would significantly boost their hopes of Champions League qualification – but also help fierce rivals Arsenal in the title race.





Some Blues supporters are poking fun at the situation, joking that Liam Rosenior should be sacked if they beat Man City.

One wrote on X: “Rosenior out if we win tomorrow.”

Another fan replied: “Even a draw should be sackable.”

A third added: “If Rosenior wins or draw tomorrow, they should sack him. It’s now an obligation to lose.”



Chelsea fans take pride in their team’s ability to step up to big occasions, in direct contrast to Arsenal who often choke in major finals.

Since Arsenal last won the league in 2004, the Blues have won the Premier League FIVE times, Champions League TWICE, Europa League TWICE, Club World Cup TWICE and Conference League ONCE.

Arsenal’s 2-1 defeat to Bournemouth means if City win all eight of their remaining matches, the title will be decided on goal difference.

City host Arsenal next Sunday needing to win to close the nine-point gap, although they have two games in hand.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chelsea are outside the top five and have ground to make up in the race for Champions League spots.

Rosenior’s honeymoon start quickly turned awry after a humiliating Champions League last-16 exit 8-2 on aggregate to Paris Saint Germain.

The former Hull City and Strasbourg head coach oversaw four straight defeats in March and some Chelsea fans are already demanding for him to be sacked just three months into his tenure.

Chelsea parted ways with former boss Enzo Maresca in December following a fall-out with Blueco, the club owners.

Despite the chatter, sources close to the club claim Rosenior’s position is not under immediate threat and will not be reviewed until the summer of 2027.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s defeat to Bournemouth is their second worst in Premier League since records began as impact of loss laid bare
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’s shock defeat to Bournemouth was one of the worst performances on record by the club in the Premier League.

The Gunners lacked firepower against the Cherries as they were downed 2-1 at the Emirates Stadium.





Viktor Gyokeres was only able to get Arsenal on the board via the penalty spot after Ryan Christie‘s handball.

The Cherries were able to put together some slick moves, with Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott both on target.

Mikel Arteta‘s side were sluggish throughout the match with only three shots on target, including the goal.

From open play, the Gunners could only muster an xG of 0.19 during the 90 minutes.

This is the club’s second-worst effort in the history of the Premier League on record, according to Opta.

The only time the North London side managed less was in the 1-0 home win over Crystal Palace in October earlier this season.

The result should not have come as a huge shock as Bournemouth manager Andoni Iraola boasts a solid record against Arteta.

The Spanish boss has beaten his counterpart on three occasions since his arrival in the Prem.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Only Pep Guardiola (seven) and Jurgen Klopp (four) have won bragging rights over Arteta more than Iraola.

Arsenal fans will be worried about the club’s recent form, which has seen them lose two of their last five at home.

This is as many as they had managed in their previous 33 league games – a run that saw them win 23, draw eight and lose two.

In all competitions, the Gunners have lost three of their last four games, the same amount as in their opening 49 games of the season.

Kroupi put himself into an exclusive club with his strike at the Emirates Stadium.



The Frenchman, 19, became just the third teenager to score in home and away matches against the Gunners in a Prem season.

He joined Kevin Gallen for Queens Park Rangers in the 1994-95 season and Wayne Rooney for Everton in 2002-03.



There was one positive from the game with Gyokeres netting his 18th goal in all competitions.

Only Thierry Henry and Alexis Sanchez managed more goals in their debut campaigns with Arsenal.

Henry leads the way with an astonishing 26 goals in the 1999-00 season, while Sanchez managed an impressive 25 in 2014-15.

Arsenal will hope the result is just a blip on their way to their first Prem title since 2003.

They will have the chance to steal back the initiative from Man City on April 19 when the two face off at the Etihad Stadium.

This comes after their Champions League quarter-final second leg against Sporting Lisbon.

Sports.title: Arsenal verdict: Gunners never believed they could turn it around against Bournemouth – what an absolute disaster
Sports.content:
WHAT an absolute disaster for Arsenal.

Alex Scott, the best player on the pitch, scored the winner as Bournemouth grabbed a 2-1 victory at the Emirates Stadium.





Eli Junior Kroupi put the Cherries ahead and Viktor Gyokeres equalised from the penalty spot, but no complaints from Arsenal.

They were really poor and it just proved, without a doubt, that the title race is still alive.

Manchester City have got to win at Chelsea, but there are lots of big questions for Mikel Arteta.

There were lots of really poor individual performances. They were uncertain at the back.

David Raya’s distribution was not great. But, moving forward, they lacked confidence.

For me, Declan Rice gave absolutely everything. He was the only player that can really hold his head high, although I thought Eberechi Eze did well when he came on as a substitute.

Arsenal were lacking in energy and belief. In the stands, there were lots of nerves.

I don’t really blame the fans, simply because the players didn’t give them enough reason to be confident.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But real credit needs to go to Bournemouth, and I think today shows that those who think games against mid-table sides in the Premier League are easy at this stage of the season really are wrong.

The Cherries played some really good football. Scott shone and it was a really good finish.

But Arsenal were opened up far too easily and Gabriel Magalhaes lost possession ahead of the goal.



The Gunners pushed at the end and Gyokeres had a couple of really good chances, but I don’t think they truly believed they could turn it around.

I think they’ll be absolutely fine in the week against Sporting in the Champions League, having taken a 1-0 lead in the first leg.

I’m sure Arsenal will be through to the semi-finals, but the big game, of course, is away to Manchester City next Sunday.

Arsenal ratings vs Bournemouth By Joshua Hall ARSENAL’S title bid took a hammer blow as they fell to a 2-1 home defeat at the hands of Bournemouth. Here’s how the players rated… DAVID RAYA – 6

A few rare mistakes for the goalkeeper, who has been one of Arsenal’s best performers this season. He was very lucky not to give away a goal on two occasions when he misplaced passes out from the back. Still made a few important saves, though. BEN WHITE – 5

His insistence on taking the best part of a minute to take a throw-in, not only frustrated the Arsenal fans inside the Emirates, but also slowed the Gunners down at times. He was also completely unaware of Adrien Truffert ghosting in behind him to set up Bournemouth’s opener. There were some bright moments in the second half, but White has struggled to fill Jurrien Timber’s shoes of late. WILLIAM SALIBA – 7

Another solid showing from the Frenchman, who is always so calm when the ball comes in his direction. His aerial ability has become so important to the way Arsenal stunt opposition attacks, too. GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 6

It was largely unfortunate that the ball deflected off the Brazilian’s toe to tee up Bournemouth’s opener. He, like Saliba, never really has an off-game, but it was his clearance that gave Bournemouth the ball back for their second goal too. MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Just a second Premier League start of the season for the full-back, who was last in the starting XI for a league game in December. You would be forgiven for thinking he might struggle by being thrown back in, but he put in very solid performance. Some nice interceptions and drives through midfield. MARTIN ZUBIMENDI – 4

When a team is as organised in their press as Bournemouth are, you need a player who can break lines and take risks to bring their team forward. Zubimendi wasn’t able to do that today, with Declan Rice having to drop in and link things up for the most part. The Spaniard was also holding onto the ball for far too long at time, slowing Arsenal down and inviting pressure. He was guilty of letting Alex Scott drift behind him for Bournemouth’s winner, too. DECLAN RICE – 7

Given the captain’s armband for today’s fixture, despite Gabriel starting the game, and he put in a captain’s performance to go with it. When Arsenal went 1-0 down, Rice was the man that wanted the ball and that was trying to carry his team forward. You always get 100 per cent from Rice, but right now he looks like his running on an empty tank. KAI HAVERTZ – 5

When Havertz is chosen in midfield it often leaves a gaping Odegaard or Eze sized hole in the Arsenal team. Although technically secure, his skillset lends itself better to playing as a centre-forward. He certainly still looks like he isn’t at full fitness yet. NONI MADUEKE – 4

Was unable to make an impact from wide areas, and took too long to whip in any balls for a hungry Viktor Gyokeres in the middle. His dancing feet are impressive, but he needs to add some consistent output to his game. He was also equally as guilty as Ben White for leaving Truffert open in the build up to Bournemouth’s opener. GABRIEL MARTINELLI – 5

Similarly to Madueke, the Brazilian was taking too long to play balls into the box. Gyokeres is so often bursting into the area, but if the balls don’t come, he won’t be able to score from them. Replaced by Trossard before the hour mark. VIKTOR GYOKERES – 7

A constant threat down the the channels when Arsenal had the ball in midfield. As well as making countless runs into the box without any winger being able to find him with a cross. Took his penalty really well to spark Arsenal into life in the game. But he had to do better when the ball fell to him inside the box later on in the second half. For more Arsenal click here.

Pep Guardiola’s side know if they win that, the title could still be theirs. So, Arsenal have got to pick themselves up from this.

But the table-toppers are missing big players, particularly Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They really miss Riccardo Calafiori at left-back. He’s a terrific player, and clearly Piero Hincapie wasn’t fully fit, which is why Myles Lewis-Skelly was handed only his second Premier League start of the season.

You could tell that he lacked belief, so it was a bad day all round for Arsenal.

Sports.title: Liverpool fans protest at Fulham match after club decision and email from chief
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans protest at Fulham match after club decision and email from chief

Liverpool supporters made their feelings clear in a protest against rising ticket prices during the Premier League match at Anfield against Fulham

View 2 Images Liverpool fans display a banner in protest to the club raising their ticket prices.

Liverpool fans made their feelings crystal clear about the club's proposed plans to increase ticket prices by protesting at today's game against Fulham. Fans unveiled a banner at the Kop end at Anfield that read 'No to ticket price increase.'

‌



They also chanted 'Shove your prices up your a***," during the first-half in their clash with the Cottagers. The protest follows an attempt from chief executive Billy Hogan to quell any unrest, writing to all of the club's season ticket holders prior to the game.

‌



Speaking ahead of the game, supporters club Spirit of Shankly said: "SUPPORTERS are angry. And they have every right to be. Liverpool FC has chosen to ignore clear, overwhelming opposition from its own supporters and push ahead with plans to increase ticket prices for the next three seasons.

‌



Arne Slot drops Liverpool future hint as he confirms summer transfer plans READ MORE :

Liverpool chief doubles down on ticket stance ahead of fan protests at Anfield READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"The open meeting online, the survey, and countless conversations all point to the same thing: fans do not accept this decision. And if the club’s owners won’t listen, then we make them. This is no longer about consultation. That opportunity has been and gone. This is about action.

"Supporter groups are already organising a coordinated response. We are doing so at speed because time is against us. But the direction is clear: protests will take place. If the club does not value supporter voices, we will make ourselves difficult to ignore.

‌



"The Supporters’ Board has formally informed the club that action is coming. Now it is on all of us to back it."

View 2 Images A flyer held by a Liverpool fan regarding the protest to rising ticket price (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool confirmed last month that ticket prices will rise in line with inflation across the next three campaigns. The Spirit of Shankly then launched a campaign titled 'not a pound in the ground', encouraging fans to spend their cash at local businesses rather than Anfield for the Fulham fixture.

‌



On Thursday, fan group Spion Kop 1906 announced that they will take down their flags and banners from the Kop End for the 'remaining fixtures'.

Hogan said: "Our matchday operating costs at Anfield have risen significantly in recent years - up 85% including Anfield Road (or 57% excluding Anfield Road) over the past decade, with utility costs up 107% over just the past four years and business rates up 286% in that same period."

The American went on to clarify that the three per cent increase would mean that for next season, an adult's general admission season ticket would cost between £1.13 and £1.42 extra per match. Hogan stated that current projections suggest the price of an adult's general admission matchday ticket would rise by between £3 and £4.50 across the full three-year period.

‌



He then justified Liverpool's pricing structure in comparison to their Premier League competitors, adding: "We have frozen general admission season ticket prices in eight of the last ten seasons. Today's cheapest Kop match ticket price is the same price now as it was 15 years ago, despite cumulative inflation across the UK economy of around 45% in that period.

"We are also operating in a league where other clubs have increased prices at a materially higher rate over the past decade. Since 2016/17, our competitors in the top six have increased ticket prices by an average of 17%, where we have increased our prices by 4% over the same period.

"No decision has been made post this three year approach and we will continue to meaningfully engage with our Supporters Board ahead of that time."

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres brings up wild excuse for Arsenal losing to Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres brings up wild excuse for Arsenal losing to Bournemouth

Viktor Gyokeres spoke to the media after Arsenal suffered a significant 2-1 defeat against Bournemouth on Saturday - and one thing he said went viral on social media

View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres reacted to Arsenal's defeat (Image: TNT Sports)

Viktor Gyokeres has been ridiculed after appearing to blame a dry pitch for Arsenal's damaging defeat against Bournemouth. The Gunners slipped up in a 2-1 loss against the Cherries on Saturday, potentially opening the door for Manchester City in the Premier League title race.

‌



Gyokeres scored from the penalty spot after a handball by Ryan Christie, but Arsenal were well beaten at home. Junior Kroupi put Bournemouth ahead early on before Alex Scott provided the winner with a cool finish after a flowing move.

‌



Arsenal's £64million summer signing had a few half-chances at the end of the match, but couldn't find a second equaliser. Defeat means City can cut the gap to six points with a win over Chelsea on Sunday before playing Arsenal next weekend at the Eithad Stadium.

‌



Gyokeres was one of the Arsenal players to face the media post-match and his interview with Match of the Day quickly caught the eye on social media. "We had some okay chances at the end," he said. "The pitch was maybe a bit dry there to be honest, so that didn't help, but of course like I said we all need to do better and take our chances."

The comments were brutal. "A bit dry? Are you being serious? It’s been dry for both teams. Come on man," one reply read. "Bro doesn't remember that's it's actually their own home," a second wrote, while a third joked: "Maybe should've poured a bottle of water on it...ah I forgot - they haven't got bottle."

‌



Gyokeres and his team-mates will now turn their attention to the second leg of their Champions League quarter-final against his old club Sporting on Wednesday, before the all-important clash with City on Sunday.

"Very confident," he said when asked about Arsenal turning their form around after three defeats in the last four games in all competitions. "I think we don't need to get stuck too much on what happened today. We need to look forward, think positive and look forward to the games."

View 2 Images Arsenal have to pick themselves up after the loss (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

‌

Gyokeres also spoke to TNT Sports after the loss. "I think we could have played much better in both halves really," he said. "We didn't control the game well enough. And they're a good side so when they get some chances, they will make it difficult for us and we had to do better there and then, of course, attacking wise do more."

Asked if Arsenal were disjointed, he replied: "Yeah, I think we had a good feeling before the game and during the game we were ready for everything, but they made it difficult for us and we made it difficult for ourselves and that's why the end result is like it is. It always hurts when you lose.

"We have a lot of games still to play and we know how good we are - we just have to show it on the pitch. We have to get back into that rhythm that we can play in and believe in ourselves."

Sports.title: Paul Merson warns Arsenal stars are 'smashed to pieces' after latest title blow
Sports.content:
Paul Merson warns Arsenal stars are 'smashed to pieces' after latest title blow

Arsenal were beaten by Bournemouth at the Emirates as they opened the door for Manchester City and Paul Merson insists they need to keep their head down in the coming days

View 2 Images Paul Merson admits the outside noise will ramp up following Arsenal's loss (Image: Sky Sports)

Paul Merson has told the Arsenal players to avoid all of the reaction to their Bournemouth loss with growing concerns they could collapse after the Premier League title race was blown wide open.

‌



The Gunners' poor run continued on Saturday as they were shocked at home by the Cherries, who extended their unbeaten run to 12 games. Alex Scott came up with a second-half winner that has put Manchester City in control of their own destiny.

‌



Arsenal have sat top for the majority of the season but have lost three of their last four games. That has seen them miss out on the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup whilst their league ambitions are now being questioned.

‌



Mikel Arteta's side let leads at the top slip in 2023 and 2024, being overhauled by City on both occasions. Now the Manchester outfit could again take charge if they win their games in hand and see off Arsenal next week - leading to talk of another collapse.

Mikel Arteta sends message to bruised Arsenal stars after painful Bournemouth defeat READ MORE :

How Man City can go top in ELEVEN days after massive Arsenal slip up READ MORE :

Merson said on Sky Sports on their confidence: "It will have been smashed it to pieces. Now all of a sudden, if Man City win all their games, they're level on points. Plus they've got two games to make the goal difference up. This is now, you've got to keep away from the press, the papers and social media because everybody will be saying 'here comes the melt'.

"That is a terrible, terrible result today. Bad performance as well. No energy, no 'let's go and take the game to Bournemouth, it was sloppy."

‌



City face Chelsea on Sunday before taking on Arsenal the following week at the Etihad - a venue Arteta has never won at as Gunners boss. Days later they face Championship-bound Burnley and wins in all three games could see them go top on goal difference. Merson though has backed the Blues to stop City winning when they face off at Stamford Bridge.

View 2 Images Arsenal's poor form continued with a loss to Bournemouth - their third reverse in four outings

Pep Guardiola's side were sensational when they beat Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final, producing a dominant display in the second-half. In their next outing they hammered Liverpool 4-0 to make the last four of the FA Cup, whilst Arsenal themselves were shocked by Southampton.

Article continues below

Arsenal, for all their progress under Arteta, have continued to cop flack for failing to land any silverware. Their FA Cup success in 2020 remains their most recent trophy and they've continued to miss out when well placed in competitions.

Sports.title: Devastated Arsenal star spotted being consoled on pitch after huge title race blow
Sports.content:
Devastated Arsenal star spotted being consoled on pitch after huge title race blow

Arsenal lost 2-1 to Bournemouth at the Emirates Stadium, offering Manchester City an opportunity to close the gap before the Gunners travel to the Etihad Stadium next weekend

View 2 Images It was a tough afternoon for Arsenal, giving Man City fresh hope in the title race

Declan Rice was seen offering support to Martin Zubimendi in Arsenal's loss to Bournemouth. The 27-year-old midfielder, who joined the Gunners from Real Sociedad for £60m in the summer, endured a nightmare afternoon at the Emirates Stadium as the Cherries cruised to a 2-1 success.

‌



Between Rice and Zubimendi, possession was surrendered 29 times throughout the encounter against Andoni Iraola's outfit. The pair delivered precious little quality in midfield - they were outclassed by Ryan Christie and Alex Scott, who were instrumental in prolonging Bournemouth's unbeaten streak to 12 matches.

‌



During the opening period, as Viktor Gyokeres lined up his penalty, a supporter posted footage to Reddit showing the moment Rice recognised Zubimendi was battling. Eager to boost his colleague's morale, the England international wrapped his arm around the Spaniard.

‌



Rice tapped Zubimendi's chest while calling out something in his ear. Myles Lewis-Skelly also offered comfort to the midfielder, as did Gabriel Magalhaes, who attempted to energise him through a brief exchange and a handshake.

Noni Madueke extended his encouragement to Zubimendi as well, clasping his hand too. Despite their collective attempts to rally the midfielder, he subsequently bore responsibility for the decisive goal, neglecting to follow his marker into the penalty area.

‌



Mikel Arteta sends message to bruised Arsenal stars after painful Bournemouth defeat READ MORE :

After a midfield turnover, Zubimendi was left flat-footed as Evanilson played in Scott, who slotted the ball past David Raya from close range to wrap up three vital points. Speaking to the press after the final whistle, Mikel Arteta described the defeat as a 'big punch in the face'.

The Arsenal manager said: "Well, extremely disappointing. It's a big punch on the face. That's what I said to the boys. And now it's about how we react to that. Because game on, you're going to require now a big speed, a lot of fight and very clear. How are we going to approach that?

"There's no grey areas. We are in, we are out. And we need to be very, very, very strong and determined to approach it in a different way than we've done today, especially when the game wasn't going our way."

‌



When asked whether he had concerns about his side's response, Arteta said: "No, because I've seen them before in many scenarios and I've seen them for nine months. But today, there were some very basic things that we did extremely bad against their team.

View 2 Images A dejected looking Martin Zubimendi

‌



"When you do that, they're going to capitalise, stretch the pitch. Again, it becomes very chaotic and very difficult to control. So, yeah, it's a lot of good things that they've done, obviously, credit to them. But I think there's a lot, a lot, a lot in our plate to look at ourselves."

Arteta added: "What I'm trying to do is give our best to the club, give the responsibility to our players. And I know if the atmosphere, the fans, the support, the energy in the stadium is the best in the world.

"We have a much better chance. I don't think that there's any other possibility to perform better than when you have that kind of support. But then we have to respond.

"And we had moments in the first half where we did it and there were other moments that we were on our level. So, yeah, we have to apologise to them and improve."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms huge Man Utd injury boost for Leeds game after suspension
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms huge Man Utd injury boost for Leeds game after suspension

Manchester United return to Premier League action on Monday when they play Leeds - and Michael Carrick has a decision to make in central defence, with Harry Maguire suspended

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has Lisandro Martinez back fit (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has confirmed that Lisandro Martinez could return from injury to replace the suspended Harry Maguire against Leeds. United return to action after 24 days on Monday but will be without Maguire after he was sent off in the 2-2 draw against Bournemouth.

‌



Martinez has missed the last five United games with a calf injury and has not played since the 1-1 draw against West Ham on February 10. But he travelled with the United squad for their four-day training camp in Ireland this week and is ready to replace Maguire, if Carrick makes the call.

‌



"It's just that call that we make," Carrick said. "We wouldn't be pushed into anything. I think it's important that the boys are ready.

‌



"So that's a decision that we'll take. He's back training, which is great, and back on the grass. But we've certainly got to make the right decision and make sure he's ready."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick reveals he is making plans for next season despite Man Utd uncertainty READ MORE :

Man Utd have major issue in summer transfer market after Antoine Semenyo snub READ MORE :

United are still without Matthijs de Ligt, leaving Martinez, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven as the only two available centre-backs for the Leeds game. Maguire received a one-match suspension for giving away a penalty in the draw at Bournemouth, but could still see that extended if found guilty of improper conduct towards fourth official Matt Donohue.

‌



Patrick Dorgu has also been on the sidelines since the 3-2 away win at Arsenal on January 25. He travelled to Ireland, but is not yet in a position to return from his hamstring injury.

De Ligt has been absent since the 2-1 win over Crystal Palace on November 30 due to a frustrating back injury. And the Netherlands international may not play again this season.

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez trained with the squad in Ireland (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"He obviously wasn't there (in Ireland)," Carrick said. "The reason he didn't come, he's not quite on the grass. Patrick came with us and Pat's at that stage a little bit further on. Matta's not quite at that stage yet, so it was important for him to continue his rehab really and try and get him back.

"It's different treatment and different exercises. He's in the gym and doing work but he's not quite on the grass and he's not ready for that yet. That's the process that unfortunately when you're injured you’ve to go through. Sometimes it happens quick quicker than others and sometimes there's things that don't quite go to plan and it's a bit slower.

"He's just at that stage where he's working through that at the moment and we're trying to get him back right."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sends message to bruised Arsenal stars after painful Bournemouth defeat
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sends message to bruised Arsenal stars after painful Bournemouth defeat

Mikel Arteta has made it crystal clear to his Arsenal players that they need to be ready to fight for the Premier League title after they opened the door for Manchester City

View 2 Images Arsenal's loss against Bournemouth could prove pivotal in the title race

Mikel Arteta has told his Arsenal stars to "stand up and go for the fight or you're out" after their loss to Bournemouth which blew the Premier League title race wide open.

‌



The Gunners came into Saturday's lunchtime kick-off having lost two of their last three games, which had seen them miss out on the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup. Those defeats have ramped up the pressure but Arsenal failed to produce the desired response.

‌



They fell behind early on against the Cherries, who took the lead for a second time through Alex Scott. His 74th minute strike would prove to be the winner as fans exited the Emirates before the final whistle.

‌



Arteta is still trying to deliver the title in north London after a number of near misses. They have held a huge advantage but, despite being nine points clear, they could see Manchester City leapfrog them inside the next fortnight if results go against them.

The Spaniard has continued to face criticism for failing to get over the line and has told his Arsenal players to find the stomach for a difficult final stretch or face being dropped.

Arsenal player ratings vs Bournemouth as FIVE stars score 2/10 in horror showing READ MORE :

How Man City can go top in ELEVEN days after massive Arsenal slip up READ MORE :

He told TNT Sports: "It has to hurt. They have to take it on the chin. You stand up and go for the fight or you're out. It's a big week. A lot at stake. We're still in a good position in both competitions."

‌



Arsenal face City next weekend in a game that could well decide the destination of the title. Before that they have the second-leg of their Champions League quarter-final against Sporting Lisbon to think about. Pep Guardiola's side don't have such a distraction and have begun clicking into gear at the right time as they bid to overhaul Arsenal in another title race.

Bournemouth extended their unbeaten run to 12 games as they won at the Emirates for the second successive season, but Arteta admitted his side were not themselves.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's side have lost three of their last four games

‌



He said: "Disappointing. It's a big punch in the face and it's about how we react now. They are a team who haven't lost for 11 games for a reason, they did a lot right.

"We were far from efficient. The first chance they had to attack the box, it's a deflection, a bad defending action and it's a goal. That's something we have to recover from. The second half you expect a different game. We did a lot of strange things today. We have been very consistent. This can happen, this is football."

Sports.title: Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri dealt new blow within hours of Mikel Arteta warning
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri dealt new blow within hours of Mikel Arteta warning

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta spoke about academy graduates Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly before the Gunners took on Bournemouth

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has spoken about Arsenal's academy players (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta indicated this week he won't hesitate to make tough decisions regarding the futures of academy products Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly. The timing proved particularly unfortunate for the former, who remained an unused substitute for Marseille on Friday evening, while the latter started just his second league game this season when Bournemouth took home all three points from north London on Saturday.

‌



Arteta's title contenders may require player sales to help balance the books during the summer window. A number of first-team players could be up for grabs, with teenagers Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly among those rumoured to be at risk of an exit.

‌



The manager acknowledged the significance of the Hale End academy in supplying talent to the senior squad. However, he equally emphasised that youngsters hold no guaranteed playing time unless they get there on merit.

‌



"It's (the academy system) part of us," Arteta said the day before the Bournemouth game. "At the end what has to define this football club is to seek for excellence and seek for the best, regardless if you're coming from the academy or abroad.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal eye summer transfer swoop for Spain star as club chief confirms offer READ MORE :

Arsenal make five stars available for transfer as Mikel Arteta issues demand to board READ MORE :

"If we can have players from Hale End, much better because the identity is there. We grow with them and they know exactly what we're looking for.

‌



"But at the end they have to earn it. Not for a week, not for a month, for years. Like anybody else, it doesn't matter what department or role you have in the club. You have to sustain performance and that has to be at the very highest level if we want to win and be where we want to be."

View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri has been out of the Arsenal team of late (Image: FREDERIC DIDES, AFP via Getty Images)

Nwaneri, 19, joined Marseille on loan for the second half of the campaign. He netted on his debut for the French side but watched manager Roberto De Zerbi depart just weeks afterwards.

‌



The attacking midfielder has been given fewer chances under De Zerbi's successor Habib Beye. He's yet to make a start under the Senegalese boss and remained on the bench throughout Friday's 3-1 victory over Metz.

Nwaneri featured on the right of a front three under De Zerbi and came on for Mason Greenwood in the recent loss to Lille - the sole occasion he's played beyond 45 minutes under Beye - after his compatriot went off injured. Greenwood returned to the starting XI against Metz despite not being completely fit and contributed two assists as Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Igor Paixao and Hamed Traore all scored.

"Yesterday, he told me he wasn't 100%, he was still in pain. This morning, he told me he was feeling much better," Beye said of Greenwood after the win.

Article continues below

"Against low blocks, we need technical players. He brought a lot to our game. He reassured me. You can see the attacking quality he provides. We'll have him back at 100% during the week."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta's 'bring your dinner' claim has harmed Arsenal's Premier League title charge
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta's 'bring your dinner' claim has harmed Arsenal's Premier League title charge

ARSENAL 1-2 BOURNEMOUTH: Mikel Arteta's Gunners suffered their third defeat in four matches in all competitions but this time around, it's a loss that could have huge implications for their Premier League title bid

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta watched his Arsenal side stumble at home to Bournemouth

It was truly hard to believe you were watching the potential Premier League champions. Arsenal were abject, short of ideas, nonchalant, sloppy, weak, devoid of character and ultimately outclassed by hard-working Bournemouth.

‌



But however poor their players were, much of this defeat must also rest with Mikel Arteta. Arsenal were merely a by-product of their overly-animated and emotional head coach, namely inside the opening 20 minutes.

‌



The Spaniard had urged Gunners supporters on Friday to "bring their lunch and dinner" to the Emirates but on the field, there was a sense of panic and that sparked restlessness and frustration in the stands.

‌



Bournemouth made smart tactical fouls to disrupt Arsenal's rhythm and Arteta was like a bubbling volcano ready to erupt as he sprung around his technical area while hassling fourth official Gavin Ward.

How Man City can go top in ELEVEN days after massive Arsenal slip up READ MORE :

Arsenal player ratings vs Bournemouth as FIVE stars score 2/10 in horror showing READ MORE :

He was so agitated, he simply could not sit still, particularly after Martin Zubimendi trickled a dismal straightforward pass out of play when attempting to find the feet of Ben White.

Moments later, the ambitious Cherries broke the deadlock through Eli Junior Kroupi after fine work from Adrien Truffert and the opener prompted a swift change change in Arteta's demeanour and Arsenal's approach.

‌



The hungry Double-chasing boss turned around to the home crowd and urged them to calm down via hand gestures.

In fairness, his team, who later equalised through Viktor Gyokeres' thunderbolt penalty, immediately became more controlled and self-assured in possession, which begged the question; why was there such desperation to blow Bournemouth away?

There's respectable substance behind Andoni Iraola's side's 12-match unbeaten streak, they are a tough nut to crack but instead of attempting to wear and grind them down, Arsenal appeared set on steamrolling them from the get-go.

‌



It was poor judgement and the approach blew up in their face as Bournemouth rose to the challenge and were bang up for disrupting Arsenal's title charge for the second successive season following a shock 2-1 victory at the Emirates last May.

View 3 Images Arsenal suffered a major defeat against Bournemouth

Additionally, video footage emerged on Friday of Arsenal playing a TikTok montage on a big screen next to their training session at London Colney in a bid to inspire the players.

‌



If Arsenal's squad is short of motivation at this stage of the campaign when they virtually had one hand on the trophy, perhaps they are in bigger trouble that we all thought.

Arteta likes to think outside of the box but this kind of motivational tool feels slightly artificial and plays into the narrative that Arsenal lack the belief required to get themselves over the line purely because they have not already done it.

Make no mistake, they are now in huge trouble following Alex Scott's well-crafted winner because Manchester City have built considerable momentum and their route directly back into the title fray is already mapped out.

‌



Beat Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Sunday and defeat Arsenal at the Etihad Stadium next weekend and they will go level on points with the Gunners if they beat Burnley on April 22.

Suddenly, Arsenal's home fixtures against Newcastle and Fulham plus away trips across London to West Ham and Crystal Palace no longer look like a formality.

Two years ago, they were heavily criticised for celebrating a goalless draw at Manchester City as come the end of the season, they fell two points short of Pep Guardiola's champions at the summit.

‌



A draw would undoubtedly be a favourable result next weekend as this time around, Arsenal lead the standings and are not part of the chasing pack but it's a dangerous game to go there and play for a point.

View 3 Images Alex Scott put Bournemouth 2-1 up with a cool finish (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

If Arsenal truly want to end their gruelling 22-year wait for Premier League title glory, only a statement win at the Etihad will do and to achieve that, you can't help but feel Arteta needs the cavalry back.

‌



Captain Martin Odegaard has endured another unspecified injury setback, Bukayo Saka has not been seen since the Carabao Cup final due to a fitness problem, Jurrien Timber has now spent one month sidelined with a groin issue while Riccardo Calafiori has not started back-to-back Premier League games since early-December.

The brutal reality is that Arsenal will now struggle to get over the line without players of such importance because those that have stepped in during their absence have struggled desperately following three defeats in the past four matches in all competitions.

A greater level of maturity, responsibility and conviction is now required if Arteta's men are to be crowned champions.
